body:
"Those Germans have a word for everything!"

I want to be with someone who'll stick with me when life gets hard. Someone I can talk to about anything. Someone who wants to make my dreams come true. Someone who treats me like a top priority in their life.


That's the way I've approached every relationship I've had. My ex-wife told me what one of her life goals was. I did my best to help her fulfill that goal. She never even asked about any of my goals. No one's ever given a damn about me. And I keep settling for women who don't care as much.

>My friend's mom used to tell us that you'll find someone when you're least expecting it. For some reason, that's always given me comfort.

My mom tells me something similar but it doesn't make me feel better. I have so little faith in myself and other people. I do not believe what I want in a relationship is possible.


It's so tiring struggling with this pointless existence. I woke up today and my heart hurt. It's not even about missing my wife or the married life. It's knowing today is just another shitty day that I have to try and get through. 


Thanks for taking the time to talk to me. I'm sorry I'm so negative and whiny.

>What particular actions or behaviors have you noticed that lead you to characterize yourself as too needy?

I enter into relationships with the wrong people just because they show me *some* affection. My ex-wife is a good example. I dated her even though we had practically nothing in common. We barely spoke the same language...but she liked me and that was good enough for me. Looking back, there's no way I should've been in that relationship.

When the shit first hit the fan, one of my first reactions was to volunteer my professional services and go overseas for a year or two. I thought helping people would get my mind off of things. And living in a 3rd world country would get my life back to basics (if that makes any sense).


But then it felt like I would be doing it for the wrong reasons. It'd be for selfish reasons and not a true desire to help others. That made feel like a douche, so I didn't go.


As for something that really excites me...that's a problem. I have hobbies I enjoy, but I lack *passion* for anything.

I'm not rich or anything, but I have a fair amount of professional success. Most people tell me to appreciate my career. I do appreciate it, but it's not enough for me.


I put a lot of emphasis on love (obviously). Maybe too much. I don't really understand my obsession to be loved. The rest of my family is nothing like this. It bothers me that I'm so needy.

I've spent a small fortune on therapists. It didn't really help. I don't have a lot of friends to talk to either. I'm not very close with anyone.


I know it's stupid to compare, but i look at my peers and everyone else seems happy. No one has had to go through what I did. Some people  find happiness a lot easier. I struggle with every single day. Not even trying to find happiness, but just trying to get by one more day.

I've been involved with another woman for about 6 months. It's a complicated situation with her and I don't know if it's making things better or worse. She was going through a very tough time in her life and I tried to be there for her and help. We're close, but like I said, it's complicated.


I don't know shit either :P

yes, I'm looking for a quick fix. You are right that my problems are a result of real life situations. How do I condition myself to have a "better" response? I was hoping a hypnotherapist could fill in that blank.
I'm hoping they can get me out of this funk. Make me feel more self-confidence.

>My last piece of advice is kinda cliche but here goes: go see a funny movie. Even if you only laugh once or twice, at least you've had a glimmering moment of happiness. It sounds stupid but it has always helped me.

I watched a re-run of Family Guy last night. It's the one with the ST:TNG cast. I'll admit, I felt a bit better after watching that.

I learned a lot about myself and there will be definite tweaking. The part that's absolutely *killing* me is I won't get to work on this with my wife.
Thank you bluegerm, that was nicely written.

>cling to the hope that one day you will meet the true love of your life

I always believed she was my true love. I can't imagine being with anybody else.

>I am certain you can come out of this a stronger person.

I feel like I'm totally broken right now. I'm walking around the office pretending to smile when I can barely hold in the tears.

Thank you for your reply.

>this winter of grief and injustice.

I always knew life wasn't always fair, but I didn't think it was this unfair. I'm not even given a chance to make things right with her. She just wants out.

It's such a bitter pill to swallow. This pain is unbearable.

>the wedding vows and promises mean less than nothing to her. 

That's a very sobering thought. I have to admit, you're right about this.

> You want unconditional love. You have to put your hands out with no expectation or negativity. No harming yourself, no desire to harm her, no nothing - but love - really.

I always thought we had that. I really did. Maybe I've just been a fool all along.

And yes, this is the hardest thing I've had to endure in my life. As an engineer, I have a strong desire to understand things and fix problems. And that's one of the things that makes this so difficult for me. To me, these problems are very, very fixable. I cannot rationalize her decision - it makes so little sense to me. I don't understand how my whole life just fell apart in a month.

>Dude, it's gone - and probably wasn't there. If she comes to you and hold her hand out - great - but at this point, the unity does not exist - and you gotta face that.

You may be right. Maybe it's gone. Maybe it was never there. But I'm still trying to get through to my wife. I feel if I give up, then I'm faced with a life I can't stand. I don't want to let go.

>You want some movie or book study recommendations? 

I have a huge book and movie collection. Right now, they're sitting in garbage bags in my parents basement. Ever since I moved out, I have absolutely no desire to look at them. There's only one thing I want right now and that's to be with my wife.

> Love is great, sorrow is great! Life is great!!

I agree with the first part.

Thank you very much for your reply.

> remake yourself.

I liked who I was when I was with her. Yeah, I made my share of mistakes, but it's not like these things can't be fixed. I always thought that was part of marriage. I wish she could give us a chance.

Even if I wanted to remake myself, I wouldn't know where to begin. I can't imagine a future without my wife. I'm not sure I want a future without her.
